intro: Silver Lake is the Eastside's living room: a reservoir to walk around, a long run of restaurants on Sunset, and some of the best bars in the city. The best stretches are Sunset Junction and the strip of Silver Lake Boulevard just south of the reservoir.

inf: The Infatuation: Best restaurants in Silver Lake
infeast: The Infatuation: Best bars on the Eastside
tobars: Time Out: Best Silver Lake bars
fodors: Fodor's: Los Feliz and Eastside bars

places.w: The neighborhood's long-running coffee bar at Sunset Junction, and a people-watching post.
places.o: A pour-over on the patio.

places.w: A 50-year-old Cuban bakery that still gets the classics right. It's small, so get there early.
places.o: Cafe cubano, pastelitos and the Cubano.

places.w: Takeout-only bagels that are pliable and chewy, with a deep bench of cured fish.
places.o: The black cod bagel, or lox with wasabi tobiko cream cheese.

places.w: An all-day spot with strong coffee and a relaxed hillside patio out back.
places.o: Breakfast burrito, fried chicken sandwich or oxtail in Japanese curry.

places.w: A leafy, light-filled Persian daytime cafe with homey cooking. Portions are small, so order several.
places.o: Barbari bread, kofteh tabrizi and the Persian mille-feuille.

places.w: A picnic-style Italian cafe with standout focaccia sandwiches.
places.o: Any focaccia sandwich and the tiramisu.

places.w: Fast, reliable Taiwanese with a line out the door for years, and almost nothing over $16.
places.o: Beef scallion pancake roll and wonton noodle soup.

places.w: Candlelit Italian with clever Brazilian twists. The room is tight, which is part of the charm.
places.o: Burrata with tomato granita, branzino in coconut sauce and bananas foster.

places.w: An indulgent French-Italian bistro in a playful yellow bungalow. The menu changes monthly.
places.o: Duck tortellini, fried sweetbreads or steak frites.

places.w: Classic bistro food in a lively, slightly grungy courtyard. Book ahead.
places.o: Steak au poivre, frisée salad and sorbet in a frozen lemon.

places.w: A tropical, club-like cevicheria with bright, vibrant seafood.
places.o: Scallops on the half shell, tai snapper ceviche and the kanpachi tostada.

places.w: An Afro-Caribbean wine bar where bar seats are often open for walk-ins.
places.o: Yuca latkes, plantain gnocchi in curry and spicy coconut mussels.

places.w: A packed, lively spot for tinned seafood, tapas and wine.
places.o: Mackerel conserva, tortilla española and grilled prawns.

places.w: Fun, inventive takes on Filipino classics, with big portions and live music on weekends.
places.o: Taro-coconut dip with focaccia and crab-stuffed tortang talong.

places.w: Polished nigiri next to crowd-pleasing rolls, which makes it work for couples and groups alike.
places.o: The omakase with toro and wagyu, or spicy tuna crispy rice.

places.w: Some of the city's best Thai in a kitschy, casual room.
places.o: Larb and a bottle of natural wine.

places.w: An Indian sports bar with screens everywhere and food people talk about for weeks. Reservations go fast.
places.o: Malai rigatoni, saag pizza and masala wings. Avoid big game nights.

places.w: Chewy, bubbly brick-oven pizza from a takeout window.
places.o: The Spicy, But Oh, So Sweet Boy.

places.w: A neighborhood oyster bar with excellent oysters and an easy, solid menu. Walk-ins welcome.
places.o: Oysters, the burger and a wedge salad.

places.w: A tiny, family-run tiki bar with strong rum drinks and a line out the door. Cash only.
places.o: Whatever the bartender's pouring when the room starts chanting.

places.w: A dive-y gay dance bar with a mixed, local crowd, cheap drinks and events in the back room that are actually fun.
places.o: Check the calendar for comedy nights.

places.w: A bright pink lesbian bar in a strip mall where the party spills onto the sidewalk most nights.
places.o: Go late on a weekend.

places.w: A doorway on Sunset that opens onto a hidden patio bar, with a little theater for live music and flamenco.
places.o: Bring a group and catch a show.

places.w: A low-lit, bohemian dive with fabric draped from the ceiling. Cash only.
places.o: A Moscow mule on a Friday or Saturday.

places.w: A German tavern open since 1959 with a big back patio.
places.o: Schnitzel, sausages and a pitcher of German beer.

places.w: A whiskey bar with more than 100 bottles behind a horseshoe bar.
places.o: A whiskey flight at happy hour.

places.w: The neighborhood's centerpiece: a loop for running, a meadow for picnics and room for dogs.
places.o: Walk the loop, then eat on the Silver Lake Blvd strip just south.

places.w: Dozens of public stairways wind through the hillsides, a way to see the neighborhood off the main streets.
places.o: Link a few for a workout with views.

places.a: Sunset Blvd at Santa Monica Blvd
places.w: Where Santa Monica Boulevard ends and the closest thing Silver Lake has to a walkable center.
places.o: Shop, get coffee and people-watch.
